# `secrets/client-exposed-env`: Secret exposed to the browser through a public env variable

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family  | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                    |
| ------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| secrets | critical         | 9.5                      | [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html), [CWE-312](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/312.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Secrets that a bundler copies into the JavaScript sent to browsers:

- Variables with a public prefix (`NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `VITE_`, `REACT_APP_`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_`,
  `NUXT_PUBLIC_`, `PUBLIC_`, `GATSBY_`, `VUE_APP_`) whose **name** says they are secret
  (`…SECRET…`, `…SERVICE_ROLE…`, `…PASSWORD…`, `…PRIVATE_KEY…`) or names a server-side
  provider credential (`…OPENAI_API_KEY`, `…STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`), or whose **value** matches
  a provider secret signature.
- These variables in every `.env*` file, including gitignored ones (the bundler reads them
  at build time either way), and their references in code (`process.env.X`,
  `import.meta.env.X`).
- Keys in `next.config` `env` and entries in Vite `define` whose names suggest a secret.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

Variables prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, REACT_APP_, EXPO_PUBLIC_ (and similar), every key in next.config `env`, and Vite `define` entries are copied as plain text into the JavaScript sent to every visitor. Anything secret placed there (a service_role key, an OpenAI key, a Stripe secret key) is public, no matter how the variable is named or where the .env file lives.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- {name} is inlined into client JavaScript, and its name says it is a secret.
- {name} is inlined into client JavaScript and looks like a server-side API credential.
- {name} is inlined into client JavaScript and may be a credential. Confirm it is meant to be public.
- {name} is inlined into client JavaScript and its value is a {provider}.
- next.config `env.{name}` is inlined into client JavaScript, and the name suggests a secret.
- Vite `define` replaces {name} with its value in client JavaScript, and the name suggests a secret.

## How to fix

Rotate the secret. Remove the public prefix and only read the variable in server code (route handlers, server actions, API routes, edge functions). The browser calls your server, and your server calls the provider. For Supabase, the browser gets only the anon/publishable key, and Row Level Security protects data.

### Vulnerable

```ts
// .env.local
NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-…

// app/chat/page.tsx ('use client')
const res = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY}` },
});
```

### Fixed

```ts
// .env.local
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-…   # no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix

// app/api/chat/route.ts (server)
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const user = await requireUser(); // authenticate before spending your quota
  const res = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY}` },
    body: JSON.stringify(await buildPrompt(req, user)),
  });
  return new Response(res.body);
}

// app/chat/page.tsx ('use client')
await fetch('/api/chat', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ message }) });
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Public by design:** the Supabase anon / publishable key, Firebase web config,
  Stripe publishable keys, analytics and map keys meant for browsers are not reported.
  A `…_KEY` name that is ambiguous is reported at low confidence with a message asking you
  to confirm it is meant to be public.
- **Config objects** (`next.config` `env`, Vite `define`) are one confidence step lower,
  because the value might be a non-secret despite the name.
- **Empty values and templates** in env files mean the variable is expected, not that it
  leaked yet. They are judged by name only.
- **Limitations:** no import graph. A server-only secret passed to a client component
  through props or a shared module is not traced. Bundler configuration that exposes
  other prefixes (`envPrefix` in Vite) is not read.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```ts
// vibeguard-ignore-next-line secrets/client-exposed-env -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the line VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  secrets/client-exposed-env: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html): Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
- [CWE-312](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/312.html): Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
